landmarks.name: Fort Zeelandia
landmarks.writeup: A historic fortress in Paramaribo, originally built by the British and later expanded by the Dutch, symbolizing colonial history.

landmarks.name: Central Suriname Nature Reserve
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its pristine tropical rainforest and biodiversity.

landmarks.name: Saint Peter and Paul Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: One of the tallest wooden structures in the Western Hemisphere, located in Paramaribo.

cultural_events.name: Maroon Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrates the culture and history of the Maroon communities with music, dance, and traditional rituals.

cultural_events.name: Keti Koti
cultural_events.writeup: Commemorates the abolition of slavery in Suriname with festivities and remembrance events.

food_writeup: Surinamese cuisine is a diverse blend of Indian, African, Indonesian, Chinese, and Dutch influences, featuring dishes like roti, pom, and peanut soup.
brief_history: Suriname was originally inhabited by indigenous peoples before becoming a Dutch colony in the 17th century. It gained independence in 1975 and has a multicultural society shaped by African, Asian, and European influences.

important_people.name: Johan Adolf Pengel
important_people.description: influential politician and former Prime Minister

current_conflicts: Suriname is generally peaceful with no significant internal or external conflicts reported as of 2024.
